info.title: otelo
info.description: Query the logs, traces, and metrics that otelo keeps. Every path but the login and the logout needs the password of `otelo init`, as the cookie `otelo_password` or as `Authorization: Bearer <password>`.

get.summary:
The attribute keys of the records of a signal and of their resources over
the retention, the most common first, with their types.

Suggests the fields, operators, values, and keywords that can go at the
cursor of a query, from the attributes and values of the retention, and
describes the field of the term the cursor is in.

parameters.description: The query as typed so far.

query when missing.

Indexes an attribute of the logs or of the spans, so a query that
compares it reads only the matching records. The indexer builds
the index within seconds.

Checks the password, and sets it as the cookie `otelo_password`, which

get.summary:
The series of one metric, or the groups of them, each in buckets of one
step with the count, the minimum, the average, the maximum, and the last
value, the rate of a counter, and the distribution of a histogram.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the metric

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
The start of the range: a duration before now, such as `1h`, or an
RFC 3339 timestamp. One hour before `until` when missing.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: The end of the range, in the form of `since`. Now when missing.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most series to return.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
The series to keep, by their attributes and resource, such as
`state = used`. Every series of the metric when missing.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description:
The length of a bucket, such as `1m`. One that makes 120 buckets at
most when missing.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description:
Which points to read: `raw`, `1m`, or `1h`. When missing, the raw
points for a range of 6 hours at most, the summaries by the minute
for one of 14 days at most, and the summaries by the hour for a longer
one, or the next of them that is still kept where the range starts.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description:
The names to group the series by, separated by commas: attributes,
`service`, or `resource.<key>`, such as `http.route,resource.host.name`.
The series with the same values of them combine into one group. Each
series is its own group when missing.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description:
Keep the N groups with the highest value over the range, and combine
the rest into one group `other`.

get.summary:
The spans that the query keeps, grouped by the values of the `by` names,
the most time first. Each group has the count, the failures, the total
time, and the latency percentiles of its spans, and the name and the
attributes of its newest span. The answer has the same numbers for all the
spans, over the range and in buckets of one step.

count.description:
How many records have the key. For resources and series, how many
resources and series.

indexed.description: Whether the key has an index.

type.description:
The JSON type of the values: `string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`,
`array`, `object`, or `mixed`.

AttributeKeys.description: The attribute keys of a signal, over the retention of the signal.

record.description:
The attributes of the records: of the logs, the spans, or the attributes
of the series.

resource.description: The attributes of the resources that sent them.

AttributeValue.description:
The value of an attribute: the `AnyValue` of OpenTelemetry.

Bytes arrive as a base64 string, as OTLP/JSON writes them, so they read
back as a string. A double that JSON cannot hold, such as NaN, is a string
too.

Attributes.description: Attributes by key, in the order of their keys.

Bucket.description: The points of one series or group in one step.

last.description:
The value of the newest point. In a group, the newest points of its
series combined.

BucketChange.description:
What the points of a step say beyond their values.

`none` for a gauge and an updown, and for a step with only the first
point of a cumulative series, which has nothing to count from. `rate` is
how much a counter grew per second: its increase between neighbouring
points, over the time between them. A value that goes down is a restart,
and the increase counts from zero. `distribution` is the merged buckets
of a histogram with percentile estimates.

CompletionKind.description: What the text of a suggestion is.

Completions.description: What can go at the cursor of a query, and what the field there holds.

oneOf.description:
The field of the term the cursor is in. Missing when the cursor is in
no term, and for an attribute that no record has.

Distribution.description:
The values a histogram series recorded in one time step: its points
merged, with the increases of cumulative points.

bounds.description:
The upper bounds of the buckets. The last bucket has no upper bound.
An exponential histogram gets the bounds of its buckets, joined until
64 of them are left.

oneOf.description:
Estimates of the median and the 90th and 99th percentiles, by linear
interpolation inside a bucket. `None` without values.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

distinct_values.description: How many distinct values the daemon knows.

has_more_values_than_listed.description:
Whether the field has more distinct values than the daemon keeps, so
`distinct_values` counts only some of them.

name.description: The field as a query writes it.

type.description:
The type of the values. Of an attribute: `string`, `int`, `float`,
`bool`, `array`, `object`, or `mixed`. Of a built-in field: `string`,
`bool`, or `duration`.

values.description:
The values, the most common first, and 10 at most. For a built-in
field with fixed values, those, in their order.

FieldBody.description: A field of a query: where it comes from, its type, and its values.

oneOf.description: A field of the query language, which every record has.

count.description: How many records have the attribute.

oneOf.description: An attribute of the resources of the records.

count.description: How many resources have the attribute.

FieldOriginBody.description:
Where a field comes from: the query language, the attributes of the
records, or the attributes of their resources.

count.description:
How many records have the value. Missing for the fixed values of a
built-in field.

text.description: The value as a query writes it.

resource.description: The attributes of the resource that sends the series.

GroupKey.description:
What a group holds.

`series` is one series, when the query groups by nothing. `values` is
the series that have these values of the names of `by`, and a name that
the series lack is missing. `other` is the groups past `top`.

IndexList.description: The attributes that have an index.

IndexedSignal.description:
The kind of record whose attributes can have an index, as the API names
it.

samples.description: Up to three different bodies, newest first.

severity.description: The highest severity number in the group.

template.description:
The body with numbers, UUIDs, hex IDs, and quoted strings replaced by
placeholders.

LogGroups.description: Log lines grouped by message template, the largest group first.

partial.description:
The range has more lines than the grouping reads, so the groups count
only the newest ones.

scanned.description: How many lines the groups count.

truncated.description: More groups exist than the limit let through.

unindexed.description: The attributes the query compares that have no index.

resource.description: The attributes of the resource that sent the line.

severity.description:
The OpenTelemetry severity number, from 1 (TRACE) to 24 (FATAL), or 0
when the source set none.

truncated.description: More lines match than the limit let through.

unindexed.description:
The attributes the query compares that have no index, so it read every
line in the range.

MetricKind.description:
How the points of a series combine over time.

A `gauge` is a value at an instant, such as a CPU share. An `updown` is a
level that goes up and down, such as the memory in use, and the series of
one metric add up. A `counter` is a total that only grows, such as the
bytes sent, and a chart shows its rate. A `histogram` is the distribution
of many values, such as request durations. A `counter` and a `histogram`
have a temporality.

MetricList.description: The series in a range, by name.

truncated.description: More series exist than the limit let through.

MetricSeries.description:
The series of one metric, or the groups of them, each in buckets of one
step.

groups.description:
The highest value over the range first: the average of a gauge and an
updown, the rate of a counter, and the sum of the values of a
histogram. The group `other` comes last.

start_at.description: The range, after the retention capped it.

step_ns.description:
The length of a bucket. A query of the summaries by the minute or by
the hour rounds the step up to whole minutes or hours.

truncated.description:
More groups match than the limit let through, or the metric has more
series than a query reads.

Percentiles.description: Percentiles of the values a histogram recorded.

Resolution.description:
Which points a metric query reads.

`raw` is the points as they arrived. `1m` and `1h` are their summaries
by the minute and by the hour, which a long range reads in fewer rows.

buckets.description: The buckets that have points, oldest first.

SeriesGroup.description:
One series, or the series of a group combined in each step.

A gauge takes their average, an updown and a counter add up, and a
histogram merges its buckets. The minimum and the maximum of series that
add up are the sums of theirs, since their points do not line up in time.

resource.description: The attributes of the resource that sends the series.

Service.description: One service in a range: its stats over time.

buckets.description: Every step of the range, oldest first.

resource.description:
The attributes of the newest resource of the service. Empty when the
range has none of its telemetry.

start_at.description: The range, after the retention capped it.

step_ns.description: The length of a bucket in nanoseconds.

ServiceBucket.description: The requests and the logs of a service in one step.

ServiceStats.description:
The requests and the logs of a service in a range. A request is a span of
the server kind with `http.request.method`.

error_logs.description: The logs of the error level and above.

spans.description: Every span of the service, of any kind.

buckets.description: Every step of the range, oldest first.

resource.description:
The attributes of the newest resource of the service that has any,
such as `telemetry.sdk.language`.

Services.description: The services that sent spans or logs in a range, the busiest first.

start_at.description: The range, after the retention capped it.

step_ns.description: The length of a bucket in nanoseconds.

truncated.description: More services sent telemetry than the limit let through.

Signal.description: The kind of record a query reads, as the API names it.

SpanEvent.description: Something that happened at one time in a span, such as an exception.

SpanGroup.description: The spans that share the values of the grouping fields.

attributes.description: The attributes of its newest span.

name.description: The span name of its newest span.

values.description:
The values of the grouping fields, by the fields as a query writes
them, such as `http.route`. A field the spans lack is missing.

SpanGroups.description:
The spans a query keeps in a range, grouped by the values of some fields,
the most time first.

buckets.description: The spans of every step, oldest first.

start_at.description: The range, after the retention capped it.

step_ns.description: The length of a bucket in nanoseconds.

truncated.description:
More groups match than the limit let through, which kept the ones
with the most time.

unindexed.description: The attributes the query compares that have no index.

SpanSort.description: The order of a list of spans, or of traces by their root span.

SpanStats.description: The count, the failures, and the durations of some spans.

oneOf.description:
Estimates of the percentiles of their durations, off by 1% at most.
`None` without spans.

Spans.description: Spans, in the order the request asked for.

truncated.description: More spans match than the limit let through.

unindexed.description: The attributes the query compares that have no index.

detail.description:
The type of a field and how many records have it, or how many records
have a value.

text.description: The text to put in place of the characters from `start` to `end`.

Temporality.description:
What a point of a series counts: `cumulative` since the series started, or
`delta` since the point before.

Trace.description: One trace: its spans by start time, and the logs that carry its ID.

truncated.description: The trace has more spans or logs than the limit let through.

resource.description: The attributes of the resource that sent the span.

status.description: The OpenTelemetry status code: 2 when the span failed.

attributes.description: The attributes of the root span, such as `http.route`.

error.description: Whether a span of the trace failed.

kind.description: The OpenTelemetry span kind of the root span.

name.description: The name of the root span.

resource.description: The attributes of the resource that sent the root span.

started_at.description: The start of the root span.

Traces.description: Traces by their root span, in the order the request asked for.

truncated.description: More traces match than the limit let through.

unindexed.description: The attributes the query compares that have no index.

ValueType.description:
The type of the values of a field. `mixed` when the values of an
attribute have more than one type, and `duration` only for a built-in
field.
